# `property-became-read-only`

Property became readOnly

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `warn` in requests, `info` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `property-became-read-only` (both directions), `property-became-read-only-in-request`, `property-became-read-only-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

`readOnly: true` was added to a property, so it is no longer part of requests.

## Why this default

In requests: clients that send it have it ignored (or rejected). In responses: nothing changes.

## Example

From test case [`property-became-read-only`](../../test/cases/property-became-read-only/): A request property became readOnly: it is no longer part of requests.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          id:
            type: string
+           readOnly: true
```

Findings:

- `property-became-read-only-in-request` · warn · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  property-became-read-only: info
```

## How to fix

Keep accepting the property in requests during a transition.
